evals.prompt:
The ledger API in production keeps restarting. Write a triage note into a file named TRIAGE.md. This is the output of kubectl -n payments-prd describe pod ledger-api-7d9f8c6b5-x2k4p:

Name:             ledger-api-7d9f8c6b5-x2k4p
Namespace:        payments-prd
Node:             pool-prd-3f9k2/10.110.0.14
Status:           Running
Controlled By:    ReplicaSet/ledger-api-7d9f8c6b5
Containers:
  ledger-api:
    Image:          registry.acme.example/ledger-api:2.3.1
    State:          Waiting
      Reason:       CrashLoopBackOff
    Last State:     Terminated
      Reason:       OOMKilled
      Exit Code:    137
    Ready:          False
    Restart Count:  7
    Limits:
      memory:  256Mi
    Requests:
      memory:  256Mi
Events:
  Type     Reason   Age                 From     Message
  ----     ------   ----                ----     -------
  Warning  BackOff  2m (x31 over 18m)   kubelet  Back-off restarting failed container ledger-api in pod ledger-api-7d9f8c6b5-x2k4p_payments-prd
evals.expected_output: TRIAGE.md whose first line is 'TRIAGE payments-prd/ledger-api-7d9f8c6b5-x2k4p', then '## Cause' with OOM_KILLED, '## Evidence' quoting the 'Reason: OOMKilled' line, and '## Next step' with 'kubectl -n payments-prd top pod ledger-api-7d9f8c6b5-x2k4p --containers'. The quote is followed by the line '(describe)', and the last line is 'Owner: @acme/payments-oncall'.
assertions: TRIAGE.md exists
The first line is exactly 'TRIAGE payments-prd/ledger-api-7d9f8c6b5-x2k4p'
There are exactly three sections, '## Cause', '## Evidence' and '## Next step', in that order
The Cause section is exactly 'OOM_KILLED'
The Evidence section is a quote line starting with '> ' that contains 'OOMKilled'
The Next step section is exactly 'kubectl -n payments-prd top pod ledger-api-7d9f8c6b5-x2k4p --containers'
The note does not suggest deleting the pod, restarting a rollout, or scaling
The Evidence section names the source of the quote on its own line as '(describe)'
The last line of the file is exactly 'Owner: @acme/payments-oncall'
